title: Moral Semantics Analysis Schema
description: Structured analysis of moral semantics in philosophical arguments. Classifies cognitivist/expressivist/prescriptivist positions, evaluates Frege-Geach problem responses, assesses truth-aptness and theoretical parsimony.

analysis_id.description: Unique identifier for this moral semantics analysis run

semantic_position.description: Precise classification of the argument's semantic theory

specific_version.description: Exact version (e.g., 'Blackburn-style quasi-realist expressivism', 'Cornell-style synthetic naturalism')

truth_aptness.description: Assessment of the argument's stance on moral truth

moral_sentences_truth_apt.description: Whether moral sentences are truth-apt under the argument's view

collapse_risk.description: Whether deflationary truth collapses the cognitivism/non-cognitivism distinction, and the argument's handling of this

frege_geach_evaluation.description: Systematic testing against the five canonical embedding contexts

tests.description: Results for each of the five canonical Frege-Geach embedding contexts

verdict.description: Whether the semantic theory passes this Frege-Geach test

overall_assessment.description: Overall adequacy of the semantic theory for Frege-Geach contexts

thick_thin_concept_analysis.description: Analysis of thick and thin moral concept distribution and its semantic implications

thick_concepts_identified.description: Thick concepts deployed in the argument (e.g., courageous, cruel, generous)

thin_concepts_identified.description: Thin concepts deployed in the argument (e.g., good, bad, right, wrong, ought)

semantic_implications.description: How the thick/thin distribution bears on semantic theory choice

semantic_parsimony.description: Assessment of theoretical parsimony relative to explanatory goals
